newsitem.title: USA: U.S., N.Korean diplomats met on apology Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S., N.Korean diplomats met on apology Friday.

text.p: U.S. and North Korean diplomats met in New York on Friday for "serious and useful" talks about the North's submarine incursion into South Korean waters, the U.S. State Department said on Saturday.
Spokeswoman Phyllis Young said she could not confirm South Korean media reports that Pyongyang will soon comply with the South's demand that it apologise for the incursion.
But Young said U.S. and North Korean diplomats met in New York on Friday. "The talks were serious and useful," she said, without giving any details of the substance of the talks.
Additional meetings were probable, she said.
The U.S. officials are pressing North Korea to make a statement about the Sept. 18 submarine incident "that satisfies" the South. Previous working-level meetings took place on Saturday and on Monday.
The submarine incident, in which 26 North Korean commandos went ashore, infuriated Seoul, which put relations with the North into a deep freeze pending an apology.
A South Korean foreign ministry official said Saturday that his country has details of an apology from Pyongyang over the incident and the affair may be settled within a day.

South Korea has demanded an apology as the price of resuming aid to the North and implementing a 1994 agreement between Washington and Pyongyang under which it will supply nuclear reactors to North Korea.
